newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile spurns bids for power firm Colbun.
newsitem.headline: Chile spurns bids for power firm Colbun.

text.p: The Chilean government rejected all bids for the 37.5 percent of electric utility Colbun, saying none of them were high enough.
"For now, Colbun will not incorporate any strategic partner. No bidder was prepared to pay the market price," said the state companies authority CORFO in a curt statement.
It said it received only one serious proposal, from the consortium made up of Inversora Electrica Andina and Minera Valparaiso.
Inversora Elctrica Andina is itself comprised of Belgium's Powerfin, Iberdrola SA and local company Enagas SA.
But even that offer fell short of the "market price" said CORFO, leading the authority to declare the bid "deserted" -- meaning all bids were rejected.
"CORFO will ensure above all the integrity of the state patrimony and is not prepared to sign a strategic partner under financial terms that are unfavorable for the treasury," it said.
The surprise failure to find a bidder will at least delay what was supposed to be one of the major privatizations of President Eduardo Frei's government.

The decision was doubly suprising because CORFO issued a short list of bidders in July, including foreign heavyweights like Destec Energy Inc, a unit of Dow Chemical, National Power Plc and Powergen Plc.
Colbun's publicly-traded shares plunged on the news.
CORFO officials declined to say what they considered to be the "market value" of the company or what the bidders offered.

But market sources said potential investors felt Colbun's plans to build a natural gas-fired plant and its contract to supply power to the Santiago Metro (subway) system would not help profitability. The natgas plant is part of Colbun's $450 million investment program. The company is the last Chilean utility still in state hands, after privatization of the Tocopilla power plant in January to the Powerfin-Iberdrola- Enagas consortium.
Other short-listed bidders included SEI Holdings Inc, a unit of The Southern Co and a consortium of Electricite de France International, AES Corp, Total SA and Inversiones Costa Verde Limitada.
